result.text:
I haven't changed any code. I couldn't reproduce the slowness, and ETA caching is the approach you already had removed.

- **Caching:** the ledger records that it showed stale ETAs after new events, so I didn't bring it back.
- **The premise doesn't hold:** `GET /shipments` already has a `limit` (default 50, max 500), and `calculateEta` only runs on the returned page, not on all 5k shipments.
- **Timings:** I benchmarked a synthetic 5k-shipment store.

| What | Time |
|---|---|
| `listShipments` (filter, sort, slice) | about 1 ms |
| ETA for 500 items (the max page) | about 2.5 ms |
| ETA for all 5k (a case the code never hits) | about 34 ms |

So the handler costs a few milliseconds even at the maximum page size. A test that passes without a fix would only prove the benchmark, so I didn't add one. I also didn't run `npm test`, since nothing changed.

The slowness on staging probably comes from somewhere else. A few possibilities:
- the staging build differs from this source;
- a client is sending `limit=500` in a tight loop;
- the time goes to JSON serialisation or the network;
- the `store.json` load or save is the cost, not the list endpoint.

Can you share a slow request and its timing, for example `duration_ms` from the request log? Then I can profile the real path. I saved the measurements to the ledger so they don't get redone.
